title: When Ground Truth Is Not Ground Truth: Automatic Labeling for Hallucination Detection
summary: Human validation compared automatic supervision labels with human assessments across hallucination-detection methods. Misclassification differed substantially by judge: QGen-9B had the lowest reported rate, while BLEURT-based labels performed worse. This is an evaluation finding, not a universal ranking across tasks.
ai_technology: Automatic supervision judges including BLEURT and QGen-9B
organization: Not stated in the abstract reviewed

evidence.tested: Across two QA datasets, two generators and five languages, human validation reported misclassification rates of 12.86% for QGen-9B and about 47% for BLEURT and BLEURT-n.
evidence.unknown: The comparison covers the study’s datasets, languages, judges and human-label protocol; rates may not transfer to other settings.
